title: Unification of Quantum Graph Properties
abstract: Many properties of classical graphs are defined in terms of subsets of the vertex set. Examples include connected components, which are subsets $X \subseteq V(G)$ such that $X \times X^c$ and $E(G)$ are disjoint, or independent sets, for which $X \times X$ and $E(G)$ are disjoint. Direct generalisations of these definitions to quantum graphs are difficult to achieve, since the natural notion of subsets of a quantum set is much too rigid. As a consequence, approaches to generalising these classical properties to the quantum setting have been eclectic. In some cases, multiple inequivalent definitions of the same notion are in use. We introduce a natural and well-motivated alternative definition of subsets of a quantum set. Building on this, we propose unified definitions of quantum graph properties as straightforward generalisations of the classical definitions. We recover this way the established notions of colourings and connected components. For independent sets and cliques, our approach suggests variations that diverge from existing definitions, but address some of their counterintuitive properties. We nevertheless show how to recover an important existing definition of independent sets in our framework.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of defining graph properties on quantum graphs by proposing a novel mathematical structure called 'Projective Subsets.' This formalism overcomes the limitations of standard set theory in the quantum setting, allowing the authors to unify definitions for concepts like independent sets and connected components. It provides a deep theoretical tool for extending classical combinatorics into non-commutative quantum structures.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a mathematically rigorous way to generalize classical graph properties (like independent sets or connected components) from standard graphs to quantum graphs.
main_result: The authors introduce 'Projective Subsets' as a necessary alternative definition for subsets of a quantum set, allowing for unified definitions of quantum graph properties that recover known results while suggesting novel variations for others.
method: The approach relies on advanced mathematical tools, including the theory of $\text{C}^*$-algebras, projective modules, and categorical methods (specifically using 2-categories) to formalize set operations in a non-commutative setting.
model_or_system: The model is the 'Quantum Graph,' whose structure is mathematically encoded using finite-dimensional $\text{C}^*$-algebras or their equivalent representation via $\dagger$-Frobenius monoids ($\dagger$-SFMs).
key_observables: Connected components, colorings, independent sets, cliques, and vertex covers.
important_parameters: The analysis is initially restricted to the finite-dimensional case ($\text{FdHilb}$), with potential generalization to infinite dimensions using von Neumann algebras.
main_assumptions: The standard definition of subsets based on Gelfand duality fails for simple quantum sets like $M_n$, necessitating the projective subset formalism.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the failure of direct generalization, proposes the Projective Subset formalism ($\text{X} \sqsubseteq \text{V}(\text{G})$), and then uses this framework to propose unified definitions for various graph properties, comparing them against existing literature.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, developing robust mathematical frameworks for generalizing classical combinatorial structures (like connectivity or independence) into quantum settings is foundational for understanding quantum information geometry and topological quantum field theories.
